items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: And Stanley Kay, the manager of Diva asked me, “Where is your clarinet?”

ctx.x: That particular moment with the vibrato for some reason made me think of Kenny Davern. You had that particular tone and he’s been a favorite of mine and so I now have another favorite with you.

I loved Kenny Davern you know. It’s kind of — he was important in my path. Because years ago I played with, I played for many years with the Diva Jazz Orchestra, an all- female big band that exists for over 25 years. And we played the Clearwater Jazz Festival, it was around the year 2000. And it was Flip Phillips’ 85th birthday and at the end of the festival in the hotel everybody played “Happy Birthday” to Flip Phillips on stage, a bunch of musicians, including Buddy DeFranco and Kenny Davern. And Stanley Kay,…

Thanks for sharing that. I love that story. And speaking of important people the tune with Paquito D’Rivera was called “And the World Weeps.” And I’ve been in a situation a couple of times in my life where I was playing next to someone I really admired or was a mentor or teacher. And I was wondering if you were thinking, because he soloed first, and beautifully, did you allow yourself to have these kind of somewhat negative thoughts like what am I going to do now? You know I would have done what he did but he…

items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Anat Cohen is mentioned as a member of the interviewee's band ('Sherrie and my band') and as an idol for young musicians, but no direct personal interaction or specific collaborative history between Stanley Kay and Anat Cohen is described in the text.

ctx.x: You and John Levy are, I think, probably the great managers to have, because you went through it. You were musicians.

Well and I always will be a musician. I will always be — I mean I managed the Hines Brothers for a long time, I did a show on Broadway. Maurice and I have been together 30 years. But if I could produce the biggest show on Broadway I’m a sideman. I will always be a musician. I would rather talk to guys and hear the story than talk to David Merrick. He doesn’t interest me. I like to talk to the guys. And sometimes they can’t drag me away because I’m laughing, talking the stories. That’s where I come from, that’s…
